newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition to hold news conference.
newsitem.headline: India coalition to hold news conference.

text.p: India's ruling United Front, which adjourned after make-or-break talks with the Congress party on Thursday, said its leaders were reviewing the political situation and would hold a news conference later in the day.

"Leaders of the United Front are reviewing the situation in the light of the talks they had with Congress leaders in the forenoon. All of them will talk to the press at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT) at UF headquarters," party spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters.

Asked to comment on a Congress decision to order party lawmakers to vote against Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government in the vote of confidence scheduled for Friday, Reddy said: "Our position is absolutely clear. There is no change of leadership. There are other issues as well."

Congress president Sitaram Kesri withdrew critical support to the minority coalition on March 30, and insisted that Deve Gowda must resign for the Congress to resume support for the coalition that came to power in June 1996.
Leaders from the Congress and the United Front adjourned after a second round of talks on Thursday in a bid to end the political crisis.
The two groups closed ranks last year to oust the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the largest group in the 545-member parliament.
